1.why: resetRecordFor requires the token's stored sessionId to match the current session and /api/reset/confirm also requires session.verifiedTokenHash to equal the token hash, so the code is verified as belonging to the requesting user/session.

2.why: A token is rejected unless record.sessionId === session.id (and it is single-use), so the same reset code does not work for any other session or user.

3.why: /api/reset/confirm only updates the current session's flags and the global passwordHash; it never invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so previously authenticated sessions remain usable.

4.why: The server is TLS-only (Bun.serve with cert/key), sets HSTS and rejects x-forwarded-proto: http, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest and relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens and the registered contact are stored as SHA-256 digests and passwords as bcrypt (cost 10), which are appropriate protections, though these are hashes rather than encryption strictly speaking.

6.why: No email message exists in this system; the simulated delivery prints the raw reset code into the requesting browser's page and Logs panel, so the claim about an email guarding data is only partially applicable.

7.why: All user inputs are trimmed, length-capped, type-checked and regex-validated (contact, token, MFA code), and JSON bodies are size-limited to 4096 bytes with shape validation.

8.why: There are no outbound redirects at all; the only simulated link is a same-page hash route (#verify?token=...) and CSP confines form-action and connect-src to 'self'.

9.why: No email templates exist, and all dynamic content including simulated delivery messages is inserted via textContent under a nonce-based CSP, so no user-supplied HTML or scripts are rendered.

10.why: Error responses are generic and leak nothing, but the visible Logs panel deliberately displays the reset token and the MFA code, so tokens are in fact shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed at runtime, but the MFA code "472913" and the initial password "Initial-Clinical!2025" are hardcoded directly in the source code.

12.why: The system ships with a working preset password (Initial-Clinical!2025) and a fixed MFA code (472913), which function as default credentials.

13.why: Reset requests (3 per 10 min), verify attempts (5 per 10 min), login failures (5 then 10-minute lockout) and MFA failures (5 then lockout) are all throttled with server-side, session-independent state.

14.why: Although the message text is generic, the /api/reset/request response includes the mockToken field only when the contact matches the registered account, so the response payload reveals whether the account exists.

15.why: Reset codes are 256-bit CSPRNG base64url values, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, single-use, 15-minute TTL, and bound to both the account contact digest and the requesting session.
